key_insight: Introduce "Context Forcing": a training strategy that closes the student–teacher gap in streaming tuning by aligning the teacher's supervision with the student's long-context rollouts, producing more temporally consistent autoregressive video generation.
problem_solved: Streaming tuning methods train long-context video generators using short-window (memoryless) teachers, creating a student–teacher mismatch that causes temporal drift, incoherence, and failures over long rollouts.
method: Context Forcing — modify supervision so the teacher's guidance is conditioned or augmented to reflect long-term history, aligning the teacher's view with the student's rollout context.
Introduce consistency/alignment objectives between teacher outputs and long autoregressive student rollouts to preserve global temporal structure during streaming tuning.
Design lightweight, memory-aware training/conditioning mechanisms that enable real-time long-context generation without prohibitive compute or latency.
impact: Enables more reliable, temporally coherent long-video generation in autoregressive models, improving real-time streaming and long-rollout applications (e.g., simulation, video assistants, content creation) for practitioners.
